root.name: Slav Indian: Kudischewitsch Gambit
root.moves: 1. d4 c6 2. Nf3 Nf6 3. c4 b5

overview: Black plays 3...b5 against the English Slav-Indian set-up. After 4.cxb5 cxb5 pawns are traded and Black has queenside space, while White can attack with Qb3, a4 or e4. The advance weakens Black's queenside, and I am unsure of the theory.

white_ideas.idea: Take on b5 and challenge with a4 or Qb3
Develop Nc3 and e4 to punish the weakened queenside

black_ideas.idea: Recapture on b5 and use the c-file

typical_structures.structure: Open c-file after cxb5 cxb5; Black b5 pawn can become a target

character.notes: Early flank advance and open c-file give unbalanced play.

gambit.notes: After 4.cxb5 cxb5 the pawns are traded, so material is level.

soundness.notes: The b5 push weakens Black's queenside.

character.reason: The early b5 push leads to unbalanced play, but it is not heavily forcing.

gambit.reason: The pawn comes straight back after cxb5 cxb5.

soundness.reason: The b5 move weakens the queenside early.

structure.reason: The c-file is half open for both sides.

plans.reason: The c-file is open after the exchange and Black has pushed his queenside pawns.
